newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria records 36,000 barrels spill in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria records 36,000 barrels spill in 1995.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell's Nigerian operation said it recorded about 36,000 barrels of oil spillage in the course of its operations last year, the national news agency reported on Wednesday.

It quoted Brian Anderson, managing director of the company, as telling an oil seminar in the southeastern city of Port Harcourt that 60 percent of spillage was due to sabotage for the purpose of claiming compensation.
Oil spillage is common in Nigeria where mutinational oil companies accuse communities in the oil-producing areas of damaging their pipelines in order to claim compensations.
The communities in turn accuse the companies of failing to replace ageing flowlines and pipelines which tend to cause spillage.
Anderson said 30 percent of the spill occurred during operations, while the rest was due to the corrosion of ageing facilities.
He did not give the figure for spill recorded in 1994.
Anderson said since 1992 his company began to take steps to reduce the volume of oil spillage to the barest minimum.

The measures, he said, included upgrading old flowstations and export terminals, replacement of flowlines older than 15 years, carrying out remedial action before leaks occurred and quicker response to spills.
Shell pumps about half Nigeria's nearly two million barrels per day of crude oil.
